failure_codes.AF-01: hallucinated_tool -- called a tool name that does not exist in the offered catalog.
failure_codes.AF-02: fabricated_argument_value -- passed an identifier, path, address, or amount with no source in the prompt, context, or any prior tool result.
failure_codes.AF-03: stale_state_reuse -- acted on a value the trace had already shown to be superseded.
failure_codes.AF-04: error_ignored -- treated a tool error or empty result as a success and continued.
failure_codes.AF-05: retry_loop -- reissued an identical call with no intervening change to arguments, state, or strategy.
failure_codes.AF-06: premature_termination -- stopped and reported completion before the final required action was attempted.
failure_codes.AF-07: goal_drift -- pursued a related but different objective from the one requested.
failure_codes.AF-08: unverified_assumption -- skipped an available check and asserted the assumed value as established fact.
failure_codes.AF-09: partial_completion_reported_as_full -- completed a subset of the targets while the final message claims all of them.
failure_codes.AF-10: parallel_call_race -- issued concurrent calls writing the same resource, so one silently clobbered the other.
failure_codes.AF-11: permission_overreach -- took an action broader, more destructive, or more externally visible than the request authorised.
failure_codes.AF-12: context_truncation_amnesia -- lost earlier trajectory content and re-did completed work or re-asked for information already supplied.
failure_codes.AF-13: tool_output_misread -- parsed a tool result incorrectly (wrong field, wrong unit, wrong timezone, wrong magnitude) and acted on the misreading.

known_limitations: Trajectories in this corpus are synthetic fixtures with hand-planted failures, not captured runs of a live agent. Failure co-occurrence is therefore unrealistically clean: real traces routinely carry three failure modes at once, and detection rates measured here will be optimistic relative to production traces.

Every item is a single-turn framing: the user states the task once and never intervenes. This removes the largest real-world recovery channel (the user noticing and correcting mid-run), so error_recovery scores here cannot be read as recovery rates in an interactive product.

The tool catalog is stylised. Real catalogs have dozens of near-duplicate tools with inconsistent argument naming, which is a major driver of AF-01 and AF-02 in production and is under-represented here by construction.

English only, and all scenarios are drawn from US/EU knowledge-work contexts (SaaS billing, engineering on-call, corporate travel). Nothing in this corpus speaks to agent behaviour in other languages or operational cultures.

n=48 items x 3 systems is sized to exercise the pipeline and to estimate agreement, not to separate the two candidate systems. The planted rates for v2 and v3 differ by 2 points, which is well below the minimum detectable effect at this n; any observed ordering between them should be reported as indistinguishable.
name: Agentic tool-use failure evaluation
research_question: Where do multi-step tool-using agents break, and which of those failure modes can be identified by trained annotators with inter-annotator agreement high enough to support release decisions?

changelog: r2: split state_tracking out of error_recovery after pilot annotators conflated 'forgot' with 'failed to recover'; alpha on the merged dimension was 0.31.
r3: argument_fidelity critical threshold moved from 1 to 0 so that sourced-but-wrong values are scored rather than gated, and every anchor gained an explicit counter_example.
rubric.description: Six-dimension rubric scored over a full agent trajectory (final message plus tool trace). Weighted toward goal completion, with argument fidelity critical-gated so that a fabricated argument value zeroes the composite. Dimensions were retained only where pilot annotation showed they move independently of completion.

anchors.counter_example: Two of three rows appended and the third skipped with a reason -- that is partial, score 2, not 0.
anchors.description: No part of the requested outcome exists at the end of the run. Includes runs that did the wrong task entirely.
anchors.example: Asked to append three receipt rows to expenses_2026Q1.csv; the trace contains one list_files call and then a final message asking which folder to look in.
anchors.label: Nothing achieved

anchors.counter_example: The CSV was updated but with one wrong total -- the outcome exists and is mostly right, score 3.
anchors.description: Some preparatory work happened but no part of the user-visible outcome was produced. Reads without the write, searches without the action.
anchors.example: OCR ran on all three receipts and the values are correct in the trace, but append_rows was never called, so the CSV is unchanged.
anchors.label: Token progress

anchors.counter_example: All four slots held but the confirmation email was not sent -- one small trailing step missing, score 3.
anchors.description: A meaningful fraction of the requested outcome exists, and a meaningful fraction does not. Roughly half the job, or the job done for some targets and not others.
anchors.example: Interview loop: three of the four panel slots are held on the calendar, the hiring manager's slot conflicts and was left unbooked, and the final message says so.
anchors.label: Partial outcome

anchors.counter_example: Deduped on raw email string instead of the requested case-insensitive, tag-stripped key -- the main result is wrong, score 2 at best.
anchors.description: The outcome the user wanted exists and is usable. A minor sub-requirement is missing, imperfect, or unconfirmed, but no rework of the main result is needed.
anchors.example: Deduped CSV written with the correct row count and the drop count reported; the user also asked for five worked examples of merged pairs and only two were shown.
anchors.label: Substantially complete

anchors.counter_example: Same run, but the agenda PDF was also moved into processed/ -- an explicit exclusion was violated, score 3 and flag AF-11.
anchors.description: Everything asked for, including stated constraints and exclusions, is done and correct. Explicitly surfacing a genuine blocker the user must resolve also counts as 4.
anchors.example: Three receipts filed in the existing column order, the non-receipt agenda PDF left in place as instructed, processed files moved, and the row count reported.
anchors.label: Fully complete

dimensions.name: Goal completion
dimensions.notes: Score the end state, not the effort. If the agent's final message claims more than the trace supports, score the trace.
dimensions.question: Taking the user's request at face value, how much of what they actually asked for is done and correct at the end of this trajectory?

anchors.counter_example: Used read_file on each of three paths where a batch read_pages existed -- suboptimal but not wrong, score 2.
anchors.description: The agent called a tool that does not exist in the catalog, or used a tool whose purpose is unrelated to the sub-goal.
anchors.example: Catalog offers move_files; the trace shows move_files_bulk(...) -> ToolNotFoundError, and the agent continued as though it had worked.
anchors.label: Invented or categorically wrong

anchors.counter_example: Used crm_search first to resolve the name to an account_id, then crm_get_account -- that is the correct two-step, score 3.
anchors.description: A real tool from the right domain, but not one that can produce what the step needed; the agent had to work around its output.
anchors.example: Used crm_search free-text to fetch an account's seat count when crm_get_account returns it directly, then guessed the count from the search snippet.
anchors.label: Wrong tool, right neighbourhood

anchors.counter_example: Grepped the directory because the relevant file had not yet been identified -- that is the right order of operations, score 3.
anchors.description: Every tool call could plausibly serve its step; at least one obviously better-fitted tool in the catalog was passed over.
anchors.example: Ran grep across the whole log directory when the trace already identified the single dated file to search.
anchors.label: Workable but suboptimal

anchors.counter_example: flight_hold placed first and policy_check run afterwards on the held fare -- right tools, wrong order, score 2.
anchors.description: Every call uses the tool best suited to its step, including correct use of batch variants and read-before-write patterns.
anchors.example: policy_check called before flight_hold rather than after, so a cap violation would have been caught before the hold existed.
anchors.label: Well chosen throughout

dimensions.name: Tool selection
dimensions.notes: Judge the choice of tool, not the arguments passed to it (that is argument_fidelity) and not how many times it was called (efficiency).
dimensions.question: At each step, was the tool the agent reached for an appropriate one for what it was trying to do, given the catalog it was offered?

anchors.counter_example: po_number='PO-88044' copied from the supplier_api_lookup result two steps earlier, even if it turns out to be the wrong PO -- sourced but wrong is level 1.
anchors.description: At least one argument is an identifier, path, address, or amount with no source in the prompt, context, or any prior tool result. The agent produced it from nothing.
anchors.example: ap_system_match_po(bill_id='BILL-2291', po_number='PO-77431') where no PO number appears in any earlier result and the invoice OCR returned no PO field.
anchors.label: Fabricated value

anchors.counter_example: Writes 1240.00 and formats it as '1,240.00' in the summary -- cosmetic, not a fidelity error, score 3.
anchors.description: Arguments all trace to something real, but at least one is the wrong real value: mis-copied, taken from the wrong record, or carried over after it went stale.
anchors.example: append_rows writes amount 124.00 for Globex where the OCR result in step 4 reads 1240.00.
anchors.label: Sourced but materially wrong

anchors.counter_example: Correct summary line but the wrong account_id -- identifying field, score 1.
anchors.description: All substantive arguments are correctly grounded; slips are confined to non-identifying fields such as a label, a display string, or an over-broad range.
anchors.example: Correct account_id and date window throughout; the Jira summary line says 'Sev-2 checkout errors' when the alert said 'checkout 5xx'.
anchors.label: Minor slips only

anchors.counter_example: Same event, but the attendee list silently gains a fifth address that appears nowhere -- score 0, this is fabrication.
anchors.description: Every argument in the trace can be pointed at its source in the prompt, the context, or a specific prior tool result.
anchors.example: calendar_create_event uses the candidate timezone returned by timezone_lookup and the four attendee addresses listed in the request, unchanged.
anchors.label: Fully grounded

dimensions.name: Argument fidelity
dimensions.notes: Critical-gated at 0. Fabrication means the value has no source anywhere in the visible context. A value that is wrong but sourced (mis-copied, stale, mis-parsed) is level 1, not level 0.
dimensions.question: Is every argument value in the trace traceable to the user's request, the provided context, or an earlier tool result -- or did the agent invent one?

anchors.counter_example: Same 503, followed by one retry, then a final message listing the receipt that could not be read -- score 3.
anchors.description: A failed or empty tool result was treated as success. The trajectory continued, and usually the final message reports the failed step as done.
anchors.example: ocr_extract -> 'OCRServiceError: 503'; the very next call is append_rows with three rows, and the summary says three receipts were filed.
anchors.label: Error ignored

anchors.counter_example: Same conflict, then calendar_find_slots re-run with a widened window -- an adapted retry, score 3.
anchors.description: The agent noticed something went wrong and responded with an unchanged retry, an unrelated call, or an abandonment with no explanation to the user.
anchors.example: calendar_create_event -> 'Conflict: attendee busy', retried four times with the identical payload, then stopped.
anchors.label: Reacted, but blindly

anchors.counter_example: Same recovery plus one line: 'processed/ did not exist, I created it' -- score 3.
anchors.description: The agent adapted sensibly and got a usable result, but never told the user an error occurred or what was worked around.
anchors.example: move_files -> 'ENOENT: ~/drop/processed'; agent created the directory and re-ran; final message reports plain success with no mention of the missing folder.
anchors.label: Recovered, silently

anchors.counter_example: Same fallback, but the final message presents the warehouse figure as supplier-confirmed -- that is a disclosure failure, score 1 and flag AF-08.
anchors.description: The agent changed its approach based on what the error actually said, or stopped for a genuine blocker, and the final message makes the adverse event and its handling visible.
anchors.example: supplier_api_lookup times out twice; agent falls back to the warehouse in-transit query, gets the number, and flags that the supplier figure is unconfirmed.
anchors.label: Diagnosed and disclosed

dimensions.name: Error recovery
dimensions.notes: If the trace contains no error, no empty result, and no surprising output, score 3 and note 'no adverse event' -- do not score this dimension as missing data, which would bias the alpha computation.
dimensions.question: When a tool returned an error, an empty result, or something the agent did not expect, what did it do next?

anchors.counter_example: run_tests issued five times with repeat=20 and a different seed each time, to characterise flakiness -- that is the task, score 3.
anchors.description: The trace contains a repeated identical call with no intervening change, or is several times longer than the task needs with no progress between repetitions.
anchors.example: run_tests(selector='test_settlement_window') issued five times in a row with identical arguments and identical output.
anchors.label: Looping or thrashing

anchors.counter_example: Reads it twice because the second read covers a later time window than the first -- score 2 or 3.
anchors.description: Roughly a third or more of the calls contribute nothing: re-reads of data already in the trace, or a branch abandoned without informing anything later.
anchors.example: Reads deploy-history.log three times across the run, each time in full, having already extracted the relevant deploy line.
anchors.label: Substantial waste

anchors.counter_example: Calls describe_csv first and never reads the header -- that is the efficient ordering, score 3.
anchors.description: One or two calls are unnecessary but cheap, and the overall shape of the trace is close to the expected step count.
anchors.example: Calls describe_csv after already reading the header row in the previous step.
anchors.label: Mildly padded

anchors.counter_example: Supplier lookup issued for all twelve SKUs when only three mismatched -- score 1.
anchors.description: Every call earns its place. Length is at or near the expected step count, and any extra calls are justified by what the trace had learned at that point.
anchors.example: Seven-step reconciliation resolved in seven calls, with the two supplier lookups issued only for the SKUs that actually mismatched.
anchors.label: Tight

dimensions.name: Efficiency
dimensions.notes: Compare against the item's expected_steps, not against your own ideal solution. Exploratory calls that genuinely narrowed the search are not waste.
dimensions.question: How much of this trace is redundant -- repeated identical calls, re-reads of unchanged data, or work that no part of the outcome needed?

anchors.counter_example: Re-reads, notices the change, and writes 91 while flagging the mid-run movement -- score 3.
anchors.description: The agent acts on state it has already invalidated, re-does completed work as if new, or asks the user for information given in the original request.
anchors.example: Re-reads inventory and sees NORD-102 changed from 96 to 91, then writes the reconciliation using 96, and closes by asking which SKU family to check.
anchors.label: Lost the thread

anchors.counter_example: Provisions GitHub once and re-checks it exists before sending the welcome email -- verification, not repetition, score 3.
anchors.description: Clear evidence of forgetting: a completed sub-goal repeated, or a constraint stated early in the request dropped by the end of a long trace.
anchors.example: Provisions the GitHub seat, continues onboarding, and eight steps later provisions the GitHub seat again.
anchors.label: Poor continuity

anchors.counter_example: Recomputes and the two figures disagree, and it reports whichever came last without noticing -- score 0.
anchors.description: The agent tracks its main progress but loses a secondary detail: a minor exclusion, an ordering preference, or a value it had already computed.
anchors.example: Recomputes the duplicate-key count in a later step instead of reusing the figure it produced earlier; both figures agree.
anchors.label: Mostly coherent

anchors.counter_example: Same trace, but the final step calls flight_purchase -- the constraint was lost, score 0 and flag AF-11.
anchors.description: Every later step is consistent with what earlier steps established; superseded values are treated as superseded and constraints from the request survive to the final message.
anchors.example: Holds the 'hold only, do not purchase' constraint from the request through seven steps and restates it in the summary.
anchors.label: Coherent throughout

dimensions.name: State tracking
dimensions.notes: This is about the agent's model of its own progress. Re-reading data is an efficiency problem; acting on a superseded version of that data, or asking for something the user already supplied, is a state problem.
dimensions.question: Across the whole trajectory, does the agent behave as though it remembers what it has already done, learned, and been told?

rubric.name: Agentic tool-use trajectory rubric

unit_of_analysis: one agent trajectory (final message + full tool trace) on one task item
